on-hl.darkNote: Not redefined in the dark scheme: the same black in both.

dark.note: Every colour token except on-hl is redefined under this media query; each colorMeta entry carries its dark value in `dark` (on-hl keeps its light value). The display swipe also changes in dark: it starts 0.62em from the top and the date takes on-hl ink.

display.purpose: Today's date heading only, on the yellow display swipe; 2rem on phone.

headline.purpose: List section headings: the two-digit number in the list ink, then the name.

title.purpose: Dialog, sheet and popover titles, and the phone bar date. The palette query and large dialog fields use this size at 400.

body.purpose: To-do titles, fields and running text, on a 20px line box in rows (1.4 elsewhere; 1.45 for notes). Buttons use 500.

label.purpose: Tags, plain dates, counts, summary and hints. Small headings 700; list names on Today rows 600; the today label 600 and late labels 700.

numeral.purpose: The two-digit list index on Today rows, in the Index and in the palette, in the list ink. Only the Today-row index adds +0.02em letter-spacing; the Index rail and palette numbers have none.

elevation.note: No shadows. Overlays use a 1px ink border; modal dialogs add a backdrop of ink at 28% (color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 28%, transparent)).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing for every transition.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Opacity and fill changes: key hints fading in, button fills, the phone bar date, the Done chevron.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The band changing colour on sync failure, and a swiped row settling back.

motion.name: pen-stroke
motion.purpose: A signifier that changes on screen is drawn in (stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0). Marks present at load stay still.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition and animation collapses, and the pen stroke is removed.

narrative.overview:
The Rapid Log is the Bullet Journal's rapid-log key, written in black fineliner on a Rhodia dotPad under the pad's orange cover band. The checkbox column is a notation column. Each state has one drawn glyph (• open, × done, > moved, < rescheduled) and each verb has one key (x, >, <), so the morning triage is a single pass down that gutter.

The density is that of a working notebook: 32px rows, 15px text, tabular figures throughout, and dates in a right margin. Colour carries meaning and nothing else. Orange is the cover. Highlighter swipes sit behind text for today (yellow), late (pink) and selection (blue). Twelve fineliner inks identify lists through their two-digit index. Everything else is black and grey ink on pad white.

The surface is flat paper: square corners, 1px ink borders, no shadows, a dot grid only in the gutter, and a dashed perforation above each list's Done. The system refuses the category's round checkbox, a sidebar of anonymous coloured dots, swipe menus of extra options, and any washi tape, stickers, hand lettering or handwriting faces.
keyCharacteristics: A signifier gutter: one drawn glyph per state, each over a real checkbox.
An orange cover band over black and grey ink on pad white.
Highlighters behind text only: yellow today, pink late, blue selection.
Twelve fineliner inks on two-digit list indexes.
One face, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, with tabular figures and weights from 400 to 800.
Square, flat and shadowless, with dots only in the gutter and a dashed perforation above Done.
Light and dark schemes from the same token names.

rules.name: The Cover Band Rule
rules.body: Orange is the notebook's cover and nothing else. It fills the band (and the browser theme colour) and never appears on text, rows, buttons or rules inside the pad. The band changes colour only when sync fails, when it turns to ink.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Highlighters are fills behind fineliner ink, never text colours. Yellow means today, pink means late, blue means selected or current, and the ink over any of them is always `on-hl` black, in both schemes.

rules.name: The Ink Identity Rule
rules.body: A list's ink colours only its two-digit index, its name on Today rows, and the > mark beside it in the move picker. Titles, tags and dates stay black and grey. Because the twelve inks repeat, the number and name identify a list; the colour alone never does.

rules.name: The One Hand Rule
rules.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the only face. Hierarchy comes from size and weight (400 body, 500 controls, 600 key caps and list names, 700 numbers and labels, 800 headings), never from a second family, a script or a handwriting face.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every numeral is tabular, set on the body and repeated on form controls, so margin dates, rail counts and two-digit indexes line up in columns.

rules.name: The Notation Column Rule
rules.body: Text starts at one gutter line, 124px on desktop and 44px on phone, for every row, list heading, capture field and empty-state line. The gutter holds only signifiers, key hints, the dot grid and the Done fold's × count at the perforation.

rules.name: The One Right Edge Rule
rules.body: On desktop every column ends 12px (`edge`) inside the main column's right side; on the phone, columns end 16px from the screen edge. Due dates are right-aligned in the 104px margin column against that edge, and a quiet button pulls its box out by 12px so that its text, not its box, meets the edge.

rules.name: The Dots-in-the-Gutter Rule
rules.body: The dot grid appears only in the gutter and in the phone's opened-row verb column, never across the page.

rules.name: The Flat Pad Rule
rules.body: No surface casts a shadow. Separation comes from a 1px ink edge, a paper tone or the 28% ink backdrop.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Every box has square corners. Curves appear only inside drawn marks: the bullet, the gutter dots, icon strokes such as the search lens and the offline arcs, and round stroke caps.

rules.name: The Real Checkbox Rule
rules.body: Every signifier is drawn over a real native checkbox that fills its cell, so a click, Space and `x` all do the same thing and assistive technology announces a checkbox.

rules.name: The Three Verbs Rule
rules.body: A row's gutter and swipe offer exactly three verbs, × done, > move and < reschedule, in that order wherever they appear: the gutter hints, the phone's opened-row stack and the phone swipe (right for ×, left for > and <). Tags and Delete live in the opened row and on their keys (t, Delete).

rules.name: The Pen Stroke Rule
rules.body: The one authored motion: when a signifier changes on screen, it is drawn in like a pen stroke over 220ms. Marks present at load stay still.

dos: Do head the log with today's date at display size on the yellow display swipe, which crosses the lower band of the letters in light mode and covers the whole word, under black ink, in dark mode.
Do keep every row on the row pitch (32px desktop, 44px phone) with a 20px line box, and let long titles wrap rather than truncate.
Do name a list by its two-digit index in its ink at 700 (800 in list headings), followed by its name, everywhere it appears: the Index, list headings, Today rows, the palette and the move picker.
Do show the × > < key hints at all times on late Today rows, on hover or focus elsewhere, and never on touch devices.
Do end every list's open rows with the dashed perforation (1px dashed `rule`) and fold Done beneath it.
Do keep sync state as plain text at the right end of the band ("saved 14:32"), and turn the whole band to ink when sync fails.
Do mark keyboard focus with a 2px ink outline; on a row, also lay the blue highlighter behind the title.
Do draw icons on a 16px grid with the fineliner stroke (1.6px, round caps and joins), rendered at 14, 16 or 18px, in the current text colour.
Do turn dialogs into full-width bottom sheets on phones, with a top border only, and give every phone target at least 44px.
donts: Don't draw a round or boxed checkbox at rest; the only box is the 1px Perforation Grey outline of the cell on hover.
Don't identify lists with anonymous coloured dots or by colour alone.
Don't add swipe actions or gutter verbs beyond ×, > and <; Tags and Delete live in the opened row and on their keys.
Don't set text in a highlighter colour, or put light ink on a highlighter.
Don't use orange anywhere inside the pad.
Don't add shadows or rounded corners.
Don't add washi tape, stickers, hand lettering or handwriting faces.
Don't spread the dot grid outside the gutter.
